summary: This is the GHQ SCAP 'Summation of Non-Military Activities in Japan', No. 14, for November 1946 (the file is labelled as a Korea summation but its content is the Japan series). It reports on the promulgation of the new Constitution on 3 November, the Yoshida Cabinet's six 'fundamental policies', and the extension of the Purge to local officials and business leaders. Part II adds the Government Section's analysis of the Constitution, the electrical workers' dispute, party manoeuvres, crime statistics and the International Military Tribunal's tenth and eleventh prosecution phases. Part III gives monthly October figures on agriculture, fisheries, coal, metals, textiles, transport, communications, labor, trade, rationing, finance and property control, with many charts. Part IV covers welfare, public health, vital statistics, education reform, religion and the press. A historian will find it useful for the constitutional transition, purge scale estimates, and detailed production, price and ration statistics of the early Occupation.
highlights: The new Constitution was formally promulgated on 3 November 1946 with the Emperor's rescript; over 100,000 people gathered at the Palace grounds, and it takes effect on 3 May 1947.

On 4 November the Cabinet announced six 'fundamental policies' (popularising the Constitution, educational reform, administrative reform, local self-government, industrial rehabilitation, labor problem), drawing partisan attacks led by the Social Democrats.

On 8 November the Government extended the 4 January Purge Directive to prefectural, city, town and village officials; the press estimated about 1,000,000 screened, 170,000 removed and roughly 100 Diet members at risk, and December local elections were postponed.

The Government rejected the Central Labor Relations Committee's compromise on the electrical workers' dispute on 6 November, prompting labor and Social Democrats to demand Cabinet resignation or Diet dissolution.
The 91st Extraordinary Diet convened on 25 November for 30 days to take up the House of Councillors election, Diet, Cabinet, Imperial House and Imperial House Economy bills.
The Emperor granted amnesty to 331,400 prisoners on 3 November; 173,776 offenses were reported in September, up 21,339 on August, and 29,021 persons were awaiting trial on 30 September.

The prosecution at the Tokyo war crimes tribunal closed its eleventh phase (US-British-Japanese relations, Pearl Harbor) on 26 November, completing the substance of its case against the 27 major defendants.

Coal output in October reached 1,756,800 metric tons, only one percent over September, while labor unrest and power shortages held industry down; Bank of Japan notes in circulation hit 74,816,000,000 yen on 30 November.

sections.title: Front matter
sections.summary: Blank Google Books pages, cover of Summation No. 14 (November 1946), University of Virginia library stamp, table of contents and the list of 100 charts, maps and graphs.

sections.title: Part I: General
sections.summary: Digest of the month: no SCAP organization change, Constitution promulgation, purge extension, Diet session, economic indicators for October and welfare and education developments.

sections.title: Section 1. Organization Under SCAP
sections.summary: A single paragraph stating there was no change in the non-military organization of General Headquarters, SCAP, during November.

sections.title: Section 2. Political Activities
sections.summary: Constitution promulgated 3 November, six-point Cabinet policy, purge extended to local officials, electrical dispute, party attacks, 91st Diet opening 25 November, amnesty for 331,400 prisoners and war crimes trials.

sections.title: Section 3. Economic Activities
sections.summary: October output: coal up, oil lowest of the Occupation, cotton yarn 20,840,000 pounds, notes in circulation 74.8 billion yen, 40 more companies designated for liquidation.

sections.title: Section 4. Social Activities
sections.summary: Welfare aid to 2,703,439 persons, Child Welfare Bureau, nationwide school lunches, education reform committee's nine-year schooling proposal, Ise Shima National Park and press comment.

sections.title: Part II: Political
sections.summary: Detailed reporting on the Constitution and its analysis, purge texts, labor and party politics, crime and prisons, legal affairs and the Tokyo tribunal's tenth and eleventh phases.

sections.title: Section 1. Government and Politics
sections.summary: Promulgation ceremonies, Government Section's analysis of the Constitution, the Cabinet's six policies, text and scope of the extended Purge, labor politics, parties, local government, Diet and Emperor.

sections.title: The Constitution
sections.summary: Ceremonies of 3 November in the House of Peers, MacArthur's statement and reactions from the Liberal, Social Democratic and Communist parties and the press.

sections.title: Analysis of the Constitution
sections.summary: Government Section's study: popular sovereignty, a limited monarchy, legislative supremacy, judicial review, the Bill of Rights and enforcement of the new Constitution.

sections.title: Government Policy
sections.summary: Text of the Cabinet's 4 November statement of six 'fundamental policies' and the partisan and press reaction to it.

sections.title: The Purge
sections.summary: 8 November extension of the Purge Directive to local officials, screening criteria and procedure, estimated purgees, postponed local elections and the plan to purge business leaders.

sections.title: Labor and Politics
sections.summary: Government rejection on 6 November of the electrical workers' compromise, demands for Diet dissolution and new labor moves by the National Congress of Industrial Unions.

sections.title: Political Parties
sections.summary: Social Democrats' all-out opposition (Katayama), revival of the Democratic League and the positions of the Co-operative Democrats, Liberals and Progressives.

sections.title: Local Government
sections.summary: 30 October conference of prefectural governors in Tokyo, decentralization, local elections and the status of large cities.

sections.title: The Diet, the Emperor, Structural and Personnel Changes
sections.summary: 91st Extraordinary Diet of 25 November and its composition, the Emperor's inspection trip and popularity, and the new council created.

sections.title: Section 2. Public Safety and Intelligence
sections.summary: Orderly strikes, black-market arrests (over 700 in two weeks), 173,776 September offenses, charts of crime rates, 29,021 awaiting trial, the amnesty rescript and fire losses.

sections.title: Section 3. Legal and War Crimes
sections.summary: Legal reform and judicial matters, occupation courts, war crimes investigation and trials, and the tribunal's tenth and eleventh phases of prosecution.

sections.title: Legal Affairs and Japanese Judicial Administration
sections.summary: Strike definition left to courts, Fulbright Law not applicable, 10 November bar convention, Lawyers' Law revision and 30 October directive removing court jurisdiction over claims against Allied nationals.

sections.title: Military Occupation Courts
sections.summary: Sendai and Kyoto provost court cases, five Allied seamen caught selling Occupation property at Enoshima, and 1,183 cases tried 21 September to 20 October.

sections.title: Investigation, Apprehension and Prosecution of War Criminals
sections.summary: Atrocity investigations by Allied divisions, 223 suspects ordered apprehended and trials in Japan and the Philippines, including the Ohugi, Nanjo and Watanabe cases.

sections.title: International Prosecution: Synopsis and Tenth Phase
sections.summary: Prosecution completed the general preparations for war phase on 1 November: military and naval preparations, illegal fortifications and testimony of Horiba.

sections.title: International Prosecution: Eleventh Phase
sections.summary: US-British-Japanese relations phase, 4 to 26 November, with State Department and Navy documents and testimony of Shirao, Tateno, Ballantine and Richardson on Pearl Harbor.

sections.title: Part III: Economic
sections.summary: Monthly production, trade, price and financial statistics, mostly October 1946, across twelve sections from agriculture to reparations.

sections.title: Section 1. Agriculture and Fisheries
sections.summary: Agrarian reform ordinances of 22 November with 630,000 posters and pamphlets, crop prospects, and October fish landings of 113,196 tons; antarctic whaling fleet departure.

sections.title: Section 2. Forestry and Mining
sections.summary: Slight decline in log and lumber output, October coal production 1,756,800 tons, lignite, lowest oil output of the Occupation and metal mining.

sections.title: Section 3. Heavy Industries
sections.summary: Coke steady at 113,000 tons, falling iron and steel, nonferrous metals, rubber, cement hit by power shortage, housing and chemicals; machinery output tied to coal and power.

sections.title: Section 4. Manufacturing
sections.summary: Canning shifting to glass because of tin plate shortage (glass pack 284 percent of July), pulp down 5.6 percent, medical supplies, electrical goods, vehicles, leather and sewing machines.

sections.title: Section 5. Textile Industries
sections.summary: October cotton yarn 20,840,000 pounds, raw silk up 6.5 percent, rayon, worsted and woolen output, held back by harvest labor loss and power curtailment.

sections.title: Section 6. Transportation and Public Utilities
sections.summary: Motor vehicles 107,845, train kilometers up to 15,948,849, rail tonnage, coastwise shipping, power rationing, Shinosomi hydro plant opened 16 October and gas capacity 77.6 percent idle.

sections.title: Section 7. Communications
sections.summary: Rising telephones, toll calls and radio licenses, facsimile telegraph authorised, Tokyo-Sendai cable, postal construction, equipment output cut by strikes and a 27,000,000 yen transfer.

sections.title: Section 8. Labor
sections.summary: Union membership 4,122,209 in 14,697 unions, Labor Standards, Unemployment Insurance and Seamen's bills, labor relations committees and disputes in theaters and Tokyo-Shibaura.

sections.title: Section 9. Imports and Exports
sections.summary: Export tables for 1 January to 31 October 1946, first postwar silk fabric and vegetable wax shipments to the United States and sample shipments to China and Hongkong.

sections.title: Section 10. Rationing and Price Control
sections.summary: 41 days' staple food supply on 31 October, rice collection three times 1945, fertilizer, doubled charcoal and firewood prices from 30 November, rents, textiles and 17 percent more violations.

sections.title: Section 11. Finance
sections.summary: Bank of Japan notes of 74,816,000,000 yen on 30 November, financial institution accounts, national debt of 227,639,000,000 yen and plan to dissolve two insurance corporations.

sections.title: Section 12. Property Control and Reparations
sections.summary: Allied property seized in Japan, SCAP Dollar Custody Account opened 4 November, looted property, six firms removed from restricted list and 40 companies designated for liquidation.

sections.title: Part IV: Social
sections.summary: Welfare, public health, vital statistics, education reform, religion, cultural monuments and the press and radio.

sections.title: Section 1. Public Health and Welfare
sections.summary: Welfare payments to 2,703,439 persons, Ministry of Welfare reorganized into 11 bureaus, repatriation, penicillin price cut to 200 yen, typhus, narcotics registration and October births of 190,727.

sections.title: Section 2. Education, Religion and Media of Expression
sections.summary: Educational Reform Committee's nine-year compulsory schooling, civic education manuals, ban on public funerals for war dead, Ise Shima National Park, cultural sites and press comment.
